metadata.icdo_version: ICD-O-3.2. morphology_entries[] is GENERATED by build/generate_group_inventory.py --group IV from ICCC-2017.sqlite joined to icdo32.sqlite, never transcribed from an option file or a diagnostic pathway document (Group 4 build contract §1, §1.1). 8683 Gangliocytic paraganglioma exists in ICD-O-3.2 only at behaviour /0 and is absent from this file (build contract §0.2). 9504 Spongioneuroblastoma is retained and flagged obsolete_term though not marked [obs] by IARC -- no current WHO entity has been shown to live on its stem (build contract §2.3, ruling D2) -- and is unreachable from any tree. 9520, 9521 and 9523 are retained and reachable only by exact-string alias, pending WHO Head and Neck Tumours 5th edition (ruling D3).

morphology_entries.coding_note: Chain terminator for the paraganglionic family: 8681, 8682, 8690, 8691, 8692, 8693 and 8700 all fall back here. WHO version recorded as "WHO 2022" (Mete O, et al. Overview of the 2022 WHO Classification of Paragangliomas and Pheochromocytomas. Endocrine Pathology 2022;33(1):90-114, PMID 35285002 -- full text read 16 Sep 2026 -- and the WHO Paediatric Tumours volume, both 2022) per build contract instruction (Group 4 build contract, pre-context table). NOTE the edition nuance recorded at contract §10.1: the fixed rule that all PPGLs (paragangliomas and pheochromocytomas) are behaviour-3 neoplasms with variable metastatic potential was already settled in the 4th edition, 2017, not the 5th: "Prior to the 2017 WHO classification (also known the 4th edition), PPGLs... were accompanied by the adjectives 'benign' or 'malignant'.... As a result, all PPGLs have been considered as malignant neoplasms with variable metastatic potential." (Mete 2022, p. 100). "WHO 2022" here names the edition that classifies and names the individual entities on this stem, not the edition that first fixed the behaviour. Mete 2022 never states an ICD-O code anywhere in the paper (contract §10.1) -- it corroborates that a current WHO entity lives on the stem; icdo32.sqlite states the number. IHC panel per Mete 2022 (pp. 96-106, full text read 16 Sep 2026): synaptophysin and chromogranin A are the general neuroendocrine markers the WHO panel recommends; GATA3 is the specific marker that separates a paraganglioma/pheochromocytoma from a neuroblastic tumour at the same site (build contract §5.1); cytokeratin is negative in both families and separates neither from the other, only both from a well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumour. PHOX2B is not listed here: Mete 2022 discusses PHOX2B only under the neuroblastoma differential (p. 108), never as a paraganglioma/pheochromocytoma marker, and PHOX2B does not separate neuroblastoma from pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma -- both are PHOX2B positive (contract §5.1, §10.1). A branch citing PHOX2B for this family must cite Manethova 2023, not WHO. 8683 Gangliocytic paraganglioma is NOT built in this file (build contract §0.2): icdo32.sqlite carries it only at behaviour /0, and ICCC-3 Group IV declares behaviour 3 only, so there is no 8683/3 to author. Independently, Mete 2022 (p. 94) confirms WHO 2022 renamed the entity "composite gangliocytoma/neuroma and neuroendocrine tumor (CoGNET)", walking it out of the paraganglioma family entirely -- both legs of the two-source test agree it is removed. 8683 appears nowhere in this file as a morphology_code or alias target; it may only be an alias input resolving to a terminal that explains why it cannot be coded here and refers the case to the registrar. Whether WHO 2022 states an ICD-O code for CoGNET is unknown -- only the Mete 2022 abstract carries the CoGNET quote with no page number; the full text (p. 94) confirms it but still states no code.

morphology_entries.imaging_features: Elevated plasma free metanephrines or 24-hour urinary fractionated metanephrines, plus catecholamines and chromogranin A, together with an imaging-demonstrated adrenal (or, for the extra-adrenal presentation, paraspinal/retroperitoneal) mass at a site consistent with pheochromocytoma. Visser MJ, et al. key-points summary, Table 4 (p. 06), names this constellation -- catecholamines and chromogranin A -- as sufficient for coding 8700/3 with no tissue diagnosis, ENCR basis of diagnosis 4. Rule 6 (p. 05): basis 4 never stands alone -- the biochemical marker must accompany a clinical diagnosis or a clinical investigation (here, the imaging finding) showing cancer, not stand alone as a laboratory abnormality.
morphology_entries.coding_note: Falls back to 8680, per ICCC-2017's placement of pheochromocytoma in subgroup IVb alongside the paragangliomas. IHC panel per Mete 2022 (pp. 96-106, full text read 16 Sep 2026): synaptophysin and chromogranin A are the general neuroendocrine markers the WHO panel recommends; GATA3 is the specific marker that separates a paraganglioma/pheochromocytoma from a neuroblastic tumour at the same site (build contract §5.1); cytokeratin is negative in both families and separates neither from the other, only both from a well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumour. PHOX2B is not listed here: Mete 2022 discusses PHOX2B only under the neuroblastoma differential (p. 108), never as a paraganglioma/pheochromocytoma marker, and PHOX2B does not separate neuroblastoma from pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma -- both are PHOX2B positive (contract §5.1, §10.1). A branch citing PHOX2B for this family must cite Manethova 2023, not WHO. DIVERGENCE, recorded not acted on (build contract §4.2): Visser's own Table 4 (p. 06) places pheochromocytoma in Group XI, not Group IV. ICCC-2017 is Layer 1 and governs, and ICCC-2017 puts 8700 in IVb -- the routing does not change. One of the two Visser Table 4 rows this group owns (with 9500): catecholamines and chromogranin A plus imaging is a valid basis-4, no-tissue diagnosis for this code alone. COMPOSITE PPGL (composite paraganglioma/pheochromocytoma): icdo32.sqlite carries "Composite pheochromocytoma" as a Related term on this stem. Mete 2022 (p. 106) reports composite PPGL is about 75% pheochromocytoma-with-ganglioneuroma and about 10% each with neuroblastoma or ganglioneuroblastoma, described in adults ("fourth to fifth decade", p. 106). A composite case's ganglioneuroma component must not be routed to the D1 behaviour_exclusion terminal (build contract §3, §6 D1) -- the composite lesion as a whole stays coded to its pheochromocytoma or paraganglioma stem, not split into an excluded benign component plus a separate malignant one. Mete 2022's own abstract writes "composite paraganglioma" while the body always writes "composite PPGL" or "composite pheochromocytoma" -- an inconsistency in the source, recorded so nobody reconciles it silently (contract §10.1).

RULING D1 (build contract §2.1, §3, §6): 9490/0 is Ganglioneuroma, benign -- the fully matured end of the neuroblastic spectrum -- and is NOT authored in this file. ICCC-3 Group IV admits behaviour 3 only, so a ganglioneuroma is not a registrable Group IV cancer. This is the group's central trap: a tree that resolves "Schwannian stroma-dominant, maturing or mature" to the 9490 stem without checking behaviour would silently emit 9490/3 Ganglioneuroblastoma for a benign tumour. The behaviour_exclusion field (contract §3, ratified by the registrar) is how the tree (Tasks 4-6) must handle this -- a branch or terminal carrying it emits no morphology_code, states the lesion is 9490/0 Ganglioneuroma, benign, and refers the decision to the registrar. Precedent: Group 3 left 8000/6 and 8000/9 unauthored for the same reason. The REDCap option file lists "Ganglioneuroma" as if it were a 9490 option string -- it is not; it is 9490/0 and is not built here (build contract §0.3). CNS NOTE (build contract §0.6): icdo32.sqlite carries synonym or related terms tying this stem to the central nervous system -- yet ICCC-3 places this code in Group IVa at every site, including the CNS, and Group III does not claim it. This reads wrong to a reviewer who expects a CNS-sited tumour to route to Group III; it is not an error, it is how ICCC-3 states the group. Do not "fix" it by adding a CNS carve-out. (Related term here is "CNS ganglioneuroblastoma".) Falls back to 9500. IHC panel per Mete 2022 (p. 108) and the sympathoadrenal differential (build contract §5.1): PHOX2B, synaptophysin and chromogranin positive; cytokeratin negative. PHOX2B does NOT separate this from pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma -- both families are PHOX2B positive; GATA3 and the sustentacular S100/SOX10 pattern are what separate them (contract §5.1, §10.1) -- do not add GATA3 to this entry's required panel, it is a paraganglioma/pheochromocytoma marker, not a neuroblastic one. Evidence: Shimada 1999 and Peuchmaur 2003 (the International Neuroblastoma Pathology Committee, INPC, classification), Monclair 2009 and Ambros 2005/2009 (the International Neuroblastoma Risk Group, INRG) -- the group's best-evidenced family, corroborated a second time by Mete 2022 Table 1 (p. 108), which independently reproduces the full INPC classification (undifferentiated, poorly differentiated, differentiating; intermixed, nodular; maturing, mature) attributed to Shimada 1999. who_version recorded WHO 2022 per the Mete 2022 / WHO Paediatric Tumours convergence; the underlying INPC criteria that actually separate this code from 9500 and from 9490/0 are Shimada 1999, predating either 2022 document.

morphology_entries.imaging_features: Elevated urinary homovanillic acid (HVA) and vanillylmandelic acid (VMA), together with an imaging-demonstrated mass at a site typical of a neuroblastic primary (adrenal, paraspinal/retroperitoneal, posterior mediastinal, or elsewhere along the sympathetic chain) consistent with neuroblastoma. Visser MJ, et al. key-points summary, Table 4 (p. 06), names this constellation -- urinary HVA and VMA -- as sufficient for coding 9500/3 with no tissue diagnosis, ENCR basis of diagnosis 4, not basis 2. Rule 6 (p. 05): basis 4 never stands alone -- the biochemical marker must accompany a clinical diagnosis or a clinical investigation (the imaging finding) showing cancer, not stand alone as a laboratory abnormality.
morphology_entries.coding_note: Chain terminator for the neuroblastic family: 9490 falls back here. One of the two Visser Table 4 rows this group owns (with 8700): urinary HVA and VMA plus imaging is a valid basis-4, no-tissue diagnosis for this code alone -- the pathway's Stage-2C constellation is a Table 4 row, not a Table 3 row (build contract §4.2). CNS NOTE (build contract §0.6): icdo32.sqlite carries synonym or related terms tying this stem to the central nervous system -- yet ICCC-3 places this code in Group IVa at every site, including the CNS, and Group III does not claim it. This reads wrong to a reviewer who expects a CNS-sited tumour to route to Group III; it is not an error, it is how ICCC-3 states the group. Do not "fix" it by adding a CNS carve-out. (Synonyms here are "Central neuroblastoma" and "CNS neuroblastoma"; "Sympathicoblastoma" is also a synonym on this stem but is marked [obs].) IHC panel per Mete 2022 (p. 108) and the sympathoadrenal differential (build contract §5.1): PHOX2B, synaptophysin and chromogranin positive (NB84 and tyrosine hydroxylase are also named at p. 108 to separate neuroblastoma from rhabdomyosarcoma, Wilms tumour, Ewing sarcoma and lymphoblastic lymphoma, but are not carried here as they are not part of the closed field's minimal panel); cytokeratin negative. PHOX2B does NOT separate this from pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma -- both are PHOX2B positive; GATA3 and the sustentacular S100/SOX10 pattern do (contract §5.1, §10.1). Evidence family: see 9490's note -- Shimada 1999, Peuchmaur 2003, Monclair 2009, Ambros 2005/2009, plus Okamatsu 2009, Ma 2021, Verly 2017 and Nakagawara 2018 (contract §10), the group's strongest-evidenced code.

who_version recorded as "ICD-O-3.2", not a WHO edition: no current WHO volume has been shown to cover this entity. Pfister SM, et al. No behaviour_exclusion terminal is built for it in this task since no tree references this stem yet; a future tree task must not silently emit 9501/3 for a benign lesion. Synonym "Diktyoma, malignant" is carried at behaviour /3 on this stem. No fallback: this is an unrelated entity to 9502, 9503 and 9504 despite the shared number range -- do not invent a chain among them to make the graph tidy (build contract, pre-context).

morphology_entries.coding_note: RULINGS D4 and D6 (build contract §2.4, §6). Verified against icdo32.sqlite 16 Sep 2026 and, at the registrar's instruction, cross-checked against both the 2019 draft workbook and the 9 Oct 2020 final source workbook so a conversion artefact or a draft-stage edit could be excluded: "Peripheral primitive neuroectodermal tumor", "Peripheral neuroectodermal tumor" and "PPNET" are verbatim ICD-O-3.2 Synonym or Related terms on 9364/3 Ewing sarcoma, NOT on this stem. They alias to 9364 with a cross-group referral (Group VIII at bone, Group IX at soft tissue), never to 9503. 9364 must not appear as a morphology_code anywhere in this file (validation rule, build contract §8 item 8) -- verified: it does not. Alias-instruction entries 30, 31 and 33 (which sent these three strings to 9503) are wrong and are overridden; entry 29 ("Neuroepithelioma" alone) stands and stays on this stem. Unqualified "PNET, NOS" / "Primitive neuroectodermal tumor, NOS" are 9473/3, Group III -- also not aliased to this stem. D6: the exact phrase "peripheral neuroepithelioma" appears nowhere in ICD-O-3.2 -- not as a term, a synonym, a see-also, an inclusion or an exclusion. 9503/3 Neuroepithelioma, NOS is its only plausible home and its only ICD-O-3.2 term (icdo32.sqlite carries no synonym or related term on this stem at all); nothing in Layer 1 confirms the assignment. Ruled: alias "peripheral neuroepithelioma" to this stem, but route it through a branch that asks whether CD99 is positive with PHOX2B and synaptophysin negative (favouring the Ewing family / 9364 instead of resolving here) before resolving to this code, with an outstanding-workup row naming CD99, PHOX2B and synaptophysin when that panel is not done. ihc_markers_exclude carries CD99 for that reason -- CD99 positivity (with PHOX2B and synaptophysin negative) argues against this code and for 9364. DUAL-GROUP with Group III (build contract §1, §2.5, §6): ICCC-3 gives this code to Group III (subgroup IIIc3, behaviour 0-1,3) across the whole of C70.0-C72.9. Outside that range -- including C80.9, unknown/ill-defined primary -- it is Group IV (IVb). See this entry's topography_routing_note for the routing rule; presentation_router.json's dual_group_rules["9501-9504"] rule currently matches only C70.9, C71.9 and C72.9 and must be extended to the full C70.0-C72.9 range now that Group III is built -- that fix is out of scope for this file (contract §2.5, §7.2). Also see the topography_routing_note for the C70.0-C72.9 / Group III split, which applies to this code independently of the D4/D6 finding above -- a peripheral-site neuroepithelioma that also tests CD99-positive still refers to Group VIII/IX on histology grounds, not to Group III on topography grounds; the two rules do not interact. Out of scope, flagged not fixed here: presentation_router.json's 9260 dual-group rule still routes a code (9260/3) that ICD-O-3.2 no longer carries at behaviour /3 -- 9260 exists only at /0, Aneurysmal bone cyst. That is a Group VIII/IX defect; record it in docs/TODO.md, do not touch it here (contract §2.4).

morphology_entries.coding_note: RULING D2 (build contract §2.3, §6). obsolete_term is true; obsolete_source is NOT an [obs] marker -- icdo32.sqlite prints "Spongioneuroblastoma" on 9504/3 with no [obs] flag, so the Group 3 [obs] test does not remove it. It is retained and flagged obsolete_term instead because no current WHO entity has been shown to live on this stem: the term is a 1948 artefact with no modern diagnostic criteria, and Pfister 2022 (the group's assigned baseline, read in full 16 Sep 2026) does not discuss it or any peripheral medulloepithelioma/neuroepithelioma entity at all (contract §10). Precedent: Group 3's thirteen obsolete_term entries, which were flagged on the [obs] ground -- this entry is flagged on the no-current-WHO-entity ground instead, which is a different finding and must not be conflated with an IARC [obs] marking. Reachable from no tree (validation rule, build contract §8 item 4) -- exists only so a historical record or an exact-string alias input carrying this term resolves. who_version recorded ICD-O-3.2, not a WHO edition. No fallback: unrelated entity to 9501, 9502 and 9503 despite the shared number range.

Outside that range -- including C80.9, unknown/ill-defined primary site -- it is Group IV (IVb). Route by topography at Stage 1: C70.0-C72.9 goes to Group III; every other Group-IV-carriable site goes to Group IV. presentation_router.json's dual_group_rules["9501-9504"] rule must extend its topography_in to the full C70.0-C72.9 range now that Group III is built (build contract §2.5) -- that fix is out of scope for this file.
morphology_entries.obsolete_source: Not an IARC [obs] marking -- icdo32.sqlite carries "Spongioneuroblastoma" on 9504/3 as a plain Preferred term, unflagged. The obsolescence finding is this build's own, made on the Group 3 test ("a code leaves the decision tree only when no current WHO entity lives on its stem"): the term is an 1948-era artefact with no modern diagnostic criteria, and no current WHO volume, including Pfister SM, et al., Cancer Discovery 2022;12(2):331-355 (PMID 34921008), the group's assigned baseline, has been shown to discuss it. Do not attribute this to IARC or cite it as an [obs] term.

Chain terminator for the olfactory family: 9520, 9521 and 9523 all fall back here, and it is the only one of the four olfactory codes a histological differential branch may resolve to (ruling D3, build contract §6). Synonym "Esthesioneuroblastoma" is carried on this stem in icdo32.sqlite, with the code reference (C30.0) printed against the term itself in the source. Manethova 2023 supplies a negative PHOX2B finding for this entity -- unlike neuroblastoma and ganglioneuroblastoma (9490, 9500), which are PHOX2B positive (build contract §5.1, §10.1), this entity is reported PHOX2B negative, recorded here in ihc_markers_exclude: a PHOX2B-positive small round cell tumour in the sinonasal region argues against this code and for a sympathetic/metastatic neuroblastic process instead. Synaptophysin and chromogranin A are carried as the general neuroendocrine markers. Veyrat (Advances in Oto-Rhino-Laryngology vol. 84, 2020, pp. 154-167, abstract only) confirms Kadish and Hyams as the two staging/grading systems in clinical use but reproduces neither table and does not state an ICD-O code. decision_trees.tree_label: Sympathoadrenal axis — adrenal gland, peripheral nerve and autonomic nervous system, retroperitoneum and mediastinum (C74.0, C74.1, C74.9, C47.0–C47.9, C48.0, C48.2, C48.8, C38.1–C38.3)

nodes.question: Sympathoadrenal-region mass — adrenal gland (C74.0, C74.1, C74.9), peripheral nerve or autonomic nervous system (C47.0–C47.9), retroperitoneum (C48.0, C48.2, C48.8), or mediastinum (C38.1–C38.3). What is actually in this patient's file, and was the specimen adequate for diagnosis?
nodes.hint: Pick the highest evidence tier present. This compartment holds two biologically distinct tumour families — the neuroblastic spectrum (neuroblastoma, ganglioneuroblastoma, ganglioneuroma) and the paraganglioma/pheochromocytoma family — plus, at the adrenal gland specifically, an epithelial differential (adrenocortical carcinoma). Record adequacy honestly: an uninterpretable specimen is not a negative one.
nodes.coding_note: ENCR basis of diagnosis is computed as the highest of codes 1-8 (0 and 9 override). ihc_counts_as 7, methylation_counts_as 8 are declared on the tree object (build contract §4.2). Only 9500/3 and 8700/3 may be assigned on imaging alone, at basis 4, and only with a biochemical marker AND the imaging finding together (Visser Rule 6, p.05) — never on imaging alone. Every other code in this tree requires tissue.

options.label: Referral letter or clinical note only — no imaging report, no laboratory result and no pathology report
Imaging report (CT/MRI) with a biochemical or catecholamine work-up documented — no tissue and no cytology
Fine-needle aspiration or core-needle cytology only — no excisional or incisional biopsy report is in the file
Definitive histology report — no immunohistochemistry performed or reported
Definitive histology WITH immunohistochemistry — any of PHOX2B, synaptophysin, chromogranin A, GATA3 or cytokeratin reported
Histology and immunohistochemistry PLUS cytogenetic or molecular testing — MYCN FISH, ALK testing, germline susceptibility gene testing, or another molecular result
A specimen was taken but the report says it is inadequate, non-diagnostic, or crush artefact only
Reviewed and NOT a neoplasm — adrenal haemorrhage, extramedullary haematopoiesis, or another non-neoplastic mass at this site
options.reason: The lesion was reviewed and is not a neoplasm. Adrenal haemorrhage in a neonate, extramedullary haematopoiesis, and other non-neoplastic causes of a sympathoadrenal-region mass are real and recurring findings at this site. No morphology code is emitted and the case leaves the registry.

nodes.question: What exactly does the referral or clinical note say?
nodes.hint: A referral naming neuroblastoma, ganglioneuroblastoma, ganglioneuroma, paraganglioma or pheochromocytoma is not evidence that it is that entity — these are exactly the differential a referring clinician guesses between. None of this tree's six codes may be assigned without at least a biochemical marker and imaging together.
nodes.coding_note: Visser Rule 5 (p.03): everything without pathology is 8000/3, which is not a Group IV code at a Group IV topography — it routes to Group XII (build contract §4.2 point 3). A referral alone, with no imaging and no laboratory result in the file, does not even reach the imaging_pathway tier, so it refers out rather than falling back to a Group IV NOS.

options.label: The note names a specific tumour (neuroblastoma, ganglioneuroblastoma, ganglioneuroma, paraganglioma, or pheochromocytoma), but no imaging report and no laboratory result are in the file
options.reason: The referral names an entity, and it is recorded verbatim on the case, but it cannot be coded from a note alone: no imaging and no biochemical marker are in the file to support even the imaging-only route. Obtain the imaging report and the catecholamine or metanephrine work-up before this case can be coded.

options.label: The note describes a mass or a suspected tumour at this site without naming a specific entity, and no imaging report and no laboratory result are in the file
options.reason: Nothing beyond a clinical note is in the file. Obtain the imaging report and the catecholamine or metanephrine work-up before this case can be coded.

options.label: Further review of the file locates an imaging report or a laboratory result (urinary catecholamine metabolites, plasma or urinary metanephrines, or chromogranin A) not accounted for above

nodes.question: No tissue exists. Which biochemical work-up does the file describe?
nodes.hint: Only two entities in this tree can be coded from imaging and biochemistry alone, and each needs its own marker set: neuroblastoma needs urinary HVA and VMA; pheochromocytoma needs plasma or urinary metanephrines, or chromogranin A. Neither marker set substitutes for the other, and a case with neither documented cannot be coded here at all.
nodes.coding_note: Visser MJ et al. key-points summary Table 4 (p.06) names these as the ONLY two Group IV entities codeable with no pathology, both at ENCR basis 4. Rule 6 (p.05): basis 4 never stands alone — routed onward to the imaging_pathway node, which requires the imaging constellation AND the biochemistry together.

options.label: Urinary homovanillic acid (HVA) and/or vanillylmandelic acid (VMA) sent — a neuroblastoma work-up
Plasma free metanephrines, 24-hour urinary fractionated metanephrines, or chromogranin A sent — a pheochromocytoma work-up
No biochemical marker was sent, or none of the above results are in the file

nodes.question: No tissue and no diagnostic biochemical marker are in the file.
nodes.hint: ENCR Rule 5 (p.03): a malignancy without pathology and without one of the two Table 4 marker sets is coded 8000/3, which is not a code this group carries. The case is referred to Group XII pending further work-up.
nodes.coding_note: Visser Rule 5. 8000 at a Group IV topography routes to Group XII under the existing 8000-8005 dual-group rule (build contract §4.2 point 3).

options.label: Refer this case to Group XII pending tissue diagnosis or a diagnostic biochemical marker
options.reason: No tissue diagnosis and no diagnostic biochemical marker (urinary HVA/VMA, or plasma/urinary metanephrines, or chromogranin A) are in the file. This cannot be coded to a specific Group IV entity. Record it provisionally under Group XII (8000/3, malignant neoplasm, NOS) pending biopsy or a completed biochemical work-up.

nodes.question: No tissue exists. Tick every imaging feature the report actually states, and answer the biochemical and diversion questions below.
nodes.hint: This is the weakest evidence this tool will emit for neuroblastoma. Both the imaging picture and the biochemistry are needed together — neither alone resolves the case (Visser Rule 6, p.05).
nodes.coding_note: Visser Table 4 (p.06): urinary HVA and VMA, together with a compatible imaging finding, is sufficient for 9500/3 at ENCR basis 4, with no tissue diagnosis. This is a Table 4 row, not a Table 3 row — the constellation is coded at basis 4, not basis 2 (build contract §4.2 point 1).
imaging_features: Suprarenal, paraspinal, retroperitoneal, or posterior mediastinal mass on CT/MRI
Calcification within the mass on CT
The mass encases adjacent vessels rather than simply displacing them
No radiographic feature suggests a benign adrenal or extra-adrenal lesion

biochemical_questions.question: Urinary homovanillic acid (HVA) elevated for age
Urinary vanillylmandelic acid (VMA) elevated for age

diversion_criteria.feature: Age 5 years or older at presentation
diversion_criteria.reason: Ninety percent of neuroblastoma presents under age 5. An older child needs tissue to exclude other causes of a retroperitoneal or mediastinal mass rather than being coded on imaging and biochemistry alone.

diversion_criteria.feature: Predominantly cystic mass, or a well-encapsulated mass with no calcification
diversion_criteria.reason: Atypical for neuroblastoma; favours a different adrenal or retroperitoneal lesion, and tissue is required.

diversion_criteria.feature: Plasma free metanephrines or 24-hour urinary fractionated metanephrines are also elevated
diversion_criteria.reason: A biochemical picture overlapping with pheochromocytoma at the same site. Tissue is required to settle which entity is present rather than coding on the stronger-looking result alone.

nodes.upgrade_path: A biopsy would confirm neuroblastoma, establish the INPC subtype (undifferentiated/poorly differentiated/differentiating, or exclude a ganglioneuroblastoma or ganglioneuroma component), and allow MYCN and ALK testing.

nodes.question: No tissue exists. Tick every imaging feature the report actually states, and answer the biochemical and diversion questions below.
nodes.hint: This is the weakest evidence this tool will emit for pheochromocytoma. Both the imaging picture and the biochemistry are needed together — neither alone resolves the case (Visser Rule 6, p.05).
nodes.coding_note: Visser Table 4 (p.06): catecholamines and chromogranin A, together with a compatible imaging finding, is sufficient for 8700/3 at ENCR basis 4, with no tissue diagnosis (build contract §4.2). DIVERGENCE recorded not acted on: Visser's own Table 4 places pheochromocytoma in Group XI; ICCC-2017 is Layer 1 and places it in IVb, and ICCC-2017 governs.
imaging_features: Adrenal mass on CT/MRI, or for an extra-adrenal presentation, a paraspinal, retroperitoneal, or organ-of-Zuckerkandl mass
T2 hyperintense ('light bulb') signal on MRI, or an intense contrast washout pattern atypical for an adrenal cortical adenoma
No radiographic feature suggests a benign adrenal cortical adenoma

biochemical_questions.question: Plasma free metanephrines elevated, OR 24-hour urinary fractionated metanephrines elevated
Serum or plasma chromogranin A elevated

diversion_criteria.reason: Paediatric pheochromocytoma is rare under age 10. An adrenal mass with catecholamine excess in a young child more often proves to be neuroblastoma, and tissue is required to be sure which it is.

diversion_criteria.feature: Urinary HVA or VMA is also elevated
diversion_criteria.reason: A biochemical picture overlapping with neuroblastoma at the same site. Tissue is required to settle which entity is present.

diversion_criteria.feature: No hereditary paraganglioma-pheochromocytoma syndrome is documented and the mass was found incidentally, with no episodic hypertension, palpitations, headache or sweating recorded
diversion_criteria.reason: An asymptomatic incidental finding with no syndromic context and no catecholamine-excess symptoms is weaker support for coding on imaging and biochemistry alone. Tissue is required.

nodes.upgrade_path: A biopsy would confirm pheochromocytoma and allow germline susceptibility gene testing (SDHB, SDHD, VHL, RET, NF1, MAX, TMEM127) to be recorded.

nodes.question: A specimen was obtained but is reported as inadequate, non-diagnostic, or crush artefact only. What is the plan?
nodes.hint: A non-diagnostic specimen cannot be coded to a Group IV entity: this group has no basis-1/2 route to a specific code, only the two Table 4 marker routes (basis 4) or tissue (basis 5, 7 or 8). Refer to Group XII rather than guessing a family.
nodes.coding_note: Visser Rule 5 (p.03): basis 1 or 2 means morphology 8000/3, except for entities in Table 3 — and ICCC-3 Group IV has no Table 3 entries at all. The Group 3 un_inadequate_specimen precedent (family NOS at basis 2) does NOT transfer here: Group III's forty-three Table 3 CNS rows permit exactly that, and Group IV's only no-pathology route is Table 4 (basis 4, and only for 9500/8700). So an inadequate specimen refers to Group XII (8000/3) rather than falling back to a Group IV code.

options.label: A repeat biopsy is already planned or pending
options.reason: No tissue diagnosis was reached, and this group has no route to a specific code without one. ENCR Rule 5 (p.03) codes the case 8000/3, malignant neoplasm, NOS, which is Group XII, not Group IV. A repeat biopsy is planned; re-code the case once a diagnostic specimen is available.

options.label: A repeat biopsy is not feasible, or the patient is lost to follow-up
options.reason: No tissue diagnosis was reached and no further tissue is expected. ENCR Rule 5 (p.03) codes the case 8000/3, malignant neoplasm, NOS, which is Group XII, not Group IV.

options.label: Residual tissue exists for further sectioning or additional stains, even though the original report was non-diagnostic

nodes.question: Only fine-needle aspiration or core-needle cytology exists — no excisional or incisional histology report is in the file. What does the cytology, with any immunocytochemistry performed, show?
nodes.hint: Cytology can support a family but cannot assess the Schwannian stroma architecture that separates neuroblastoma from ganglioneuroblastoma, nor the anatomic detail full histology gives. Code to the more general stem and say why.
nodes.coding_note: ENCR basis 5 (cytology). Both outcomes here are deliberately capped at the family/NOS stem: neither the INPC subtype (9490 vs 9500) nor the site-specific paraganglioma code (8700/8681/8693) can be read off cytology alone.

options.label: Small round cell / neuroblastic pattern, with immunocytochemistry showing PHOX2B, synaptophysin and chromogranin A positive and GATA3 negative or not done
options.upgrade_path: An excisional biopsy would establish the INPC subtype (ganglioneuroma, intermixed ganglioneuroblastoma, or nodular/composite ganglioneuroblastoma) and allow MYCN and ALK testing, none of which cytology can assess.

options.label: Paraganglioma/pheochromocytoma pattern, with immunocytochemistry showing GATA3 positive
options.upgrade_path: An excisional or core biopsy would confirm the anatomic detail needed to assign the site-specific code (adrenal pheochromocytoma versus extra-adrenal sympathetic paraganglioma) and allow germline susceptibility gene testing.

options.label: Cytology is non-diagnostic, discordant, or immunocytochemistry was not performed

nodes.question: Tick each marker's result as the report states it.
nodes.hint: GATA3 is the marker that separates the paraganglioma/pheochromocytoma family from the neuroblastic family. PHOX2B, synaptophysin and chromogranin A are positive in BOTH families and do not by themselves separate them. Cytokeratin is negative in both — a positive result points away from this tree's differential entirely.
nodes.coding_note: Build contract §5.1, §10.1: PHOX2B does not separate neuroblastoma from pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma; both are PHOX2B positive (Ma Y et al., J Neuropathol Exp Neurol 2021;80(12):1108-16, for the neuroblastoma side; Manethova M et al., Virchows Arch 2023;482(4):679-86, for the paraganglioma side). Mete O et al. 2022 (pp.96-106) states the WHO paraganglioma/pheochromocytoma panel as INSM1, synaptophysin, chromogranin, keratins negative, then GATA3, tyrosine hydroxylase, dopamine beta-hydroxylase, choline acetyltransferase, with SOX10/S100 for sustentacular cells — PHOX2B is not on it. The first rule below routes an adrenal, cytokeratin-positive, GATA3-negative result to the adrenocortical carcinoma differential (ICCC-2017 subgroup XIa, ICD-O-3.2 8370/3, verified against ICCC-2017.sqlite groups.group_id 92), never to a code in this file.

resolution_logic.reason: Cytokeratin-positive and GATA3-negative in an adrenal mass points away from a neuroblastic or paraganglionic tumour of this group and towards adrenocortical carcinoma. Refer to Group XI and to the registrar to confirm cortical versus medullary origin.

nos_fallback.reason: Neither the paraganglioma/pheochromocytoma marker (GATA3 positive) nor the confirmatory neuroblastic panel (PHOX2B, synaptophysin and chromogranin A positive with GATA3 negative) was demonstrated. Coded to the tree's default, Neuroblastoma, NOS, pending a fuller immunohistochemical panel or expert pathology review.

nodes.question: What does the file say about germline or somatic genetic testing for this pheochromocytoma or paraganglioma?
nodes.hint: This does not change the morphology code. Record it for the case file.
nodes.capture_label: Germline susceptibility gene testing (SDHB, SDHD, VHL, RET, NF1, MAX, TMEM127) and any somatic molecular result — record as stated. Germline results are constitutional and determine surveillance; they do not change the morphology code.
nodes.coding_note: Build contract §0.1 challenge 7, §5.1/§E: germline testing is constitutional, not somatic, and determines surveillance, not the code. molecular_freetext per the contract's explicit instruction; no new node type.

nos_fallback.reason: Genetics capture step; this fallback is not expected to fire since the single resolution rule always advances to site resolution.

nodes.question: The histology and immunohistochemistry confirm the paraganglioma/pheochromocytoma family. Where does the tumour arise?
nodes.hint: 8700 Pheochromocytoma is the adrenal-medullary member of this family; 8681 Sympathetic paraganglioma is its extra-adrenal counterpart at a sympathetic-chain site. Every site this tree owns outside the adrenal gland (peripheral nerve/autonomic nervous system, retroperitoneum, mediastinum) is a sympathetic-chain location, not a parasympathetic one — parasympathetic sites (carotid body, vagal, jugulotympanic) belong to a different tree entirely.
nodes.coding_note: icdo32.sqlite: 8700/3 Pheochromocytoma, NOS (adrenal); 8681/3 Sympathetic paraganglioma; 8693/3 Extra-adrenal paraganglioma, NOS (Related terms Nonchromaffin paraganglioma NOS, Laryngeal/Vagal paraganglioma, Composite paraganglioma belong to parasympathetic head-and-neck sites, not this tree); 8680/3 Paraganglioma, NOS is the fully NOS chain terminator. Build contract §5, §5.1.

options.label: Adrenal medulla (C74.0, C74.1, or C74.9)

Extra-adrenal sympathetic-chain site — retroperitoneal or paraspinal (C48.0, C48.2, C48.8), posterior mediastinal (C38.1-C38.3), or a peripheral nerve/autonomic nervous system site (C47.0-C47.9) consistent with a sympathetic paraganglion
An extra-adrenal site as above, but the report does not state whether the paraganglion is sympathetic or another type
The site is not clearly documented as either the adrenal medulla or a specific paraganglion

nodes.question: What INRG stage is recorded in the file — L1, L2, M, or MS?
nodes.hint: This does not change the morphology code. Record it for the case file.
nodes.capture_label: INRG stage (L1, L2, M or MS) as stated in the file
nodes.coding_note: Monclair T et al., J Clin Oncol 2009;27(2):298-303 (INRG staging). Build contract §E: capture only, never a coding input.

nos_fallback.reason: Staging capture step; this fallback is not expected to fire since the single resolution rule always advances to molecular capture.

nodes.question: What does the file say about MYCN amplification status, ALK mutation status (germline or somatic), or any other molecular or cytogenetic result?
nodes.hint: None of this changes the morphology code. Record it for the case file.
nodes.capture_label: MYCN amplification status, ALK status, and any other molecular result — record as stated
nodes.coding_note: Build contract §E: MYCN amplification (~20% of neuroblastomas, the major prognostic marker) and ALK (germline and somatic) both change no code; molecular_freetext per the master schema, no new node type.

nos_fallback.reason: Molecular capture step; this fallback is not expected to fire since the single resolution rule always advances to histology subclassification.

nodes.question: What does the histology report describe about ganglion cell differentiation and Schwannian stromal content?
nodes.hint: This is the International Neuroblastoma Pathology Committee (INPC) classification. Stroma-poor tissue composed of neuroblasts is neuroblastoma; stroma-rich tissue with ganglion cells intermixed throughout is ganglioneuroblastoma, intermixed; a distinct neuroblastic nodule within a ganglioneuroma or intermixed background is ganglioneuroblastoma, nodular; a uniformly mature, stroma-dominant tumour with no neuroblastic component anywhere is ganglioneuroma, which is benign and outside this group. Answer from what the report states, not from grade or differentiation detail the code does not need.
nodes.coding_note: Shimada 1999; Peuchmaur 2003 (INPC); Mete O et al. 2022 Table 1 (p.108), an independent second WHO-published reproduction of the same INPC classification (build contract §10.1); WHO Paediatric Tumours Supplementary Table S3 (Pfister 2022, per build contract table): Ganglioneuroma (maturing/mature) = 9490/0; Ganglioneuroblastoma, intermixed = 9490/3; Neuroblastoma (undifferentiated/poorly differentiated/differentiating) = 9500/3; Ganglioneuroblastoma, nodular (and other composite neuroblastic tumors) = 9490/3. Option D is the D1 behaviour_exclusion branch (build contract §2.1, §3, ratified registrar ruling D1); its wording requires the report to exclude BOTH a neuroblastic component AND a paraganglioma/pheochromocytoma component, so a composite case is directed to option E and can never reach the exclusion (build contract 'THE TRAP').

options.label: A single, uniform pattern throughout — Schwannian stroma-poor, composed of neuroblasts at any level of differentiation (undifferentiated, poorly differentiated, or differentiating) — with no ganglion cells and no Schwannian stroma-rich or mature component described anywhere
options.upgrade_path: MYCN and ALK testing, where performed, are recorded but do not change this code.

options.label: Schwannian stroma-rich tissue with ganglion cells intermixed throughout, and no separate nodule or composite component described

One or more distinct neuroblastic nodules within a ganglioneuroma or intermixed-ganglioneuroblastoma background (ganglioneuroblastoma, nodular), or another composite neuroblastic tumour, all within a single specimen

A fully mature or maturing ganglioneuroma — Schwannian stroma-dominant, uniformly matured ganglion cells throughout — and the report explicitly states there is NO neuroblastic component anywhere (no undifferentiated, poorly differentiated, or differentiating foci) and NO separate paraganglioma or pheochromocytoma component

behaviour_exclusion.reason: A fully matured ganglioneuroma is a benign tumour. It has no code in this Group IV list, which only covers cancers. Record the diagnosis as ganglioneuroma and refer this case to the registrar for a coding decision.

options.label: The report describes more than one distinct tumour type in this specimen — for example, ganglioneuroma tissue together with a separate paraganglioma or pheochromocytoma component, or with a separately distinguishable neuroblastoma/ganglioneuroblastoma component that is not simply a nodule within the same lesion
Schwannian stroma content or ganglion cell maturation is not described, or the pattern does not clearly match any of the above from the report as written

nodes.question: The report describes more than one distinct tumour type in this specimen, together with ganglioneuroma tissue. What is the second, separately distinguishable component?
nodes.hint: This question exists because a specimen containing ganglioneuroma tissue is not necessarily a ganglioneuroma: WHO recognises composite phaeochromocytoma-ganglioneuroma and composite phaeochromocytoma-ganglioneuroblastoma as their own entities, and a nodular neuroblastic component within a ganglioneuroma is a ganglioneuroblastoma, nodular, not a ganglioneuroma. Code to the composite entity, not to the ganglioneuroma component alone.
nodes.coding_note: WHO Paediatric Tumours Supplementary Table S3 (Pfister 2022, per build contract table): 'Ganglioneuroblastoma, nodular (and other composite neuroblastic tumors)' is 9490/3. Mete 2022 p.106: composite PPGL is ~75% pheochromocytoma-with-ganglioneuroma and ~10% each with neuroblastoma/ganglioneuroblastoma; icdo32.sqlite carries 'Composite pheochromocytoma' as a Related term on 8700/3 and 'Composite paraganglioma' as a Related term on 8693/3. This node is the trap-prevention gate required by build contract §B: it is reached ONLY from sa_histology_subclassification's composite option, so a composite case can never reach the D1 behaviour_exclusion branch.

options.label: The second component is a paraganglioma or pheochromocytoma
The second component is a neuroblastoma or a ganglioneuroblastoma
options.upgrade_path: Recorded as Ganglioneuroblastoma per the WHO composite/nodular neuroblastic tumour category. MYCN and ALK testing, where performed, are recorded but do not change this code.

options.label: The report describes more than one component but does not specify what the second component is
options.upgrade_path: A fuller pathology description of both components would allow this composite tumour to be coded to its specific entity rather than to the tree's default.
